description:
REWRITTEN 2026-09-04 after the crude column was made to work (op-190j.2). The original version of this bead over-claimed: it listed three solver defects, and two of them turned out to be MY modelling errors, not the port's.

What was actually wrong with the model, not the solver:
  * feeding the column pseudo-components boiling past 800 K, which cannot vaporise at 1.2 bar — fixed with a residue cut point that bypasses them to the bottoms, as a refinery does
  * side draws specified as absolute rates that exceeded the internal reflux once the bypass shrank the column feed — fixed by expressing draws as fractions of the column feed
With both fixed, Wang-Henke converges in 38 iterations to a monotonic, physically sensible CDU profile. Sum-Rates was not retried after the fix and may well work too; that is worth checking before assuming it is broken.

WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY WRONG WITH THE PORT, and why this bead stays open:

1. WANG-HENKE REPORTS SUCCESS ON A NON-PHYSICAL PROFILE. This is the important one. Both of my modelling errors produced a *converged* result with a small residual (2.0e-7 and 6.7e-7) and a temperature profile that DIPPED mid-column — a column cannot get colder going down. The solver has no monotonicity check on its converged profile, so a wrong answer is indistinguishable from a right one by its return value alone. Adding that check would have turned two silent wrong answers into two honest failures, and would have saved most of the debugging. Recommend: assert monotonicity of the converged temperature profile in the solver itself, or at minimum surface it as a warning on the output.

2. NO PR78. The heaviest generated pseudo-component has omega = 1.16; standard Peng-Robinson's kappa correlation is stated only for omega < 0.49, and PengRobinson + Wang-Henke fails with non-finite K-values at the feed stage. PR78 exists precisely for heavy components and is not in PropertyPackageModel (Ideal / PengRobinson / Srk). Any serious petroleum work needs it — the crude column currently runs on ideal K-values, which is adequate for a teaching model and not for anything else.

Downgraded P1 -> P2 since the blocking symptom is resolved.
title: columns: Wang-Henke reports success on a non-physical profile; PropertyPackageModel has no PR78

notes.content:
3 of 4 BCs fully ported (agent pass, 2026-07-15) under src/genfoam/thermal_hydraulics/boundary_conditions/:
- blackbody_radiation.rs (317 LOC): BlackBodyRadiationBc — Stefan-Boltzmann wall temp from a Fourier heat-flux estimate. 4 tests incl. 3 V&V (closed-form Stefan-Boltzmann inversion, hand-computed Fourier flux, composed full-step), all passing.
- velocity_rundown.rs (208 LOC): VelocityRundownBc — power-law pump/flow coastdown U(t)=U0*(A+B*(t-t0))^C. 3 tests incl. 1 V&V (hand-computed power-law factor), all passing.
- time_field_table.rs (299 LOC): TimeFieldTable — per-face time-tabulated scalar BC; reuses ScalarInterpolateTable (one instance per face column) rather than new math. 6 unit tests, all passing.
- nusselt_baffle.rs (180 LOC): NusseltThermalBaffle1DBc — SCAFFOLD ONLY, data-shape + unimplemented!() methods. Not ported: the master/slave implicit cross-patch coupling doesn't fit the "pure closure" contract used here; needs op-p6p.7.11 (porous solver) to land first to decide how inter-patch coupling is represented. Follow-up bead needed for the real port.

Verification: whole-crate build is currently broken by concurrent sibling edits (multi_region/mesh_region.rs, thermal_hydraulics/solver/one_phase.rs — not touched by this bead). Built + ran all 22 tests green (incl. clippy clean, Android aarch64-linux-android check clean) in an isolated scratch crate mirroring the real module tree/deps, since cargo test -p outram-foam-appbuilder-lib couldn't run end-to-end. Re-run cargo test -p outram-foam-appbuilder-lib --lib --release boundary_conditions once sibling breakage clears, to confirm in-tree.

Not yet done: full NusseltThermalBaffle1D port (this bead's remaining scope, or split to a follow-up bead).

title: genfoam TH: boundary conditions

description:
Mirrors GitHub issue #32 (https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/32), maintainer: 'kovan-cli should import the token savings features of kopitiam-cli, by wiring the api in directly. then we shld be able to have kovan-cli generate skill.md also for AI agents to read. Then after this, use kovan-cli for token saving features and dogfood.'

SURVEYED 2026-08-22 (read-only, ~/Documents/fun_projects/kopitiam per the workspace's consume-binaries-only rule -- this epic is about depending on specific published LIBRARY crates from that workspace, not the kopitiam/kopi-beans BINARIES the hard rule is about):

1. TOKEN COST ESTIMATE. kopitiam's 'kopitiam tokens <path>' is backed by kopitiam-tokenizer (published, AGPL-3.0-only, deps: kopitiam-core + regex + serde_json -- all lightweight, no C/BLAS/GPU) -- specifically estimate::estimate_tokens(text: &str) -> usize and estimate_tokens_by_line, a dependency-free per-Unicode-script character-weighted estimator (~25-30% accuracy vs real BPE, deliberately -- see its own module doc). kovan's own token-estimation today is kovan-semantics::agent_docs::estimated_tokens(bytes) = bytes/4 -- a much cruder heuristic, used only by 'kovan-cli agent-docs-gen --budget'. Issue #32's 'wiring the api in directly' matches the precedent already set by kopitiam-pdf (crate-local dependency in crates/kovan/Cargo.toml, never the workspace table, since kovan is already this workspace's one AGPL-3.0-only crate) -- NOT a port, a direct dependency, same boundary-exception shape.

2. OUTLINE / SLICE. kopitiam's 'outline'/'slice' are richer (rust-analyzer-backed, via kopitiam-semantic) but kovan-semantics ALREADY has ripgrep-first single-file primitives that cover the same job at the ripgrep tier: LanguageAdapter::rough_definition_pattern() + kovan_discovery::search_file(path, pattern) -> Vec<SearchMatch{line, column, text}>. No new dependency needed for a first cut -- this is a 'kovan already has 90% of this' case per the workspace's search-before-building rule.

3. SKILL.MD. kopitiam has scripts/gen-kopitiam-skill.sh -> kopitiam_skill.md (Claude Code Skill frontmatter + 'CRITICAL agent guidance' + recipes + command reference, ~1132 lines, shell-script-generated). Per this workspace's own 'no Python/scripts for documentation generation -- build it into kovan' hard rule (spirit extends to shell here too, and kovan already self-generates docs via 'kovan agent-docs-gen'/'kovan api-docs'), kovan-cli's equivalent should be a native subcommand, not a companion script.

4. CHECK/TEST --compact (diagnostics dedup, kopitiam's diagnostics.rs, ~1053 lines) and richer LSP-backed outline/refs/callers/callees (kopitiam-semantic, rust-analyzer-backed) are bigger pieces, deliberately deferred to follow-on child beads -- not blocking the first cut.
title: kovan-cli token savings — import kopitiam-cli's token-frugal features, generate skill.md, dogfood
